idiom_name: frozen snapshot objects in an array + Array.prototype.findLast as-of lookup
implementation_notes: JavaScript expresses the roles with object literals: the continuity is an object or class holding an array of { effective, snapshot } entries, and each snapshot is a frozen object created by spread-copying the previous one, so 'immutable published version' is Object.freeze plus copy-on-write instead of a class. The as-of lookup is Array.prototype.findLast (ES2023) over entries ordered by effective time - the array is the temporal collection and the reverse scan is a stdlib method; for long histories keep a parallel array of epoch milliseconds and binary-search that. Date stays an epoch-milliseconds instant and the TC39 Temporal API changes only the date algebra, not the continuity/version structure.
pitfalls: Object.freeze is shallow: nested objects and arrays stay mutable and can rewrite published history - deep-freeze or copy nested structures on publish.

Date is an instant displayed in local time: comparing timezone-less date strings or mixing local and UTC inputs shifts effective dates by a day near midnight - normalize to epoch milliseconds or ISO-8601 UTC.
Array.prototype.sort compares strings by default and sorts in place, so a missing numeric comparator leaves the history unordered (and findLast wrong) for every holder of the array.
Writes to frozen objects fail silently in sloppy mode and throw in modules, so a forgotten copy surfaces as unchanged history rather than as an error - assert the appended version in tests.
